sections.label: Section 43-22-1 - Definitions
sections.text:
As used in this chapter, the term:
(1)
"Junk" means any used article of commerce which is composed principally of iron, steel, brass, copper, zinc, or their alloys, or any other base metals and which is commonly bought for the purpose of resale or refabrication, or both.
(2)
"Junk dealer" means any person, firm, or corporation or officer, agent, or employee of any person, firm, or corporation who engages in the purchase of junk for the purpose of resale or refabrication, or both.

sections.label: Section 43-22-2 - Registration with judge of probate court
sections.text:
No person, firm, or corporation or employee of any person, firm, or corporation shall engage in the business of purchasing junk in any county of this state without first registering his name with the judge of the probate court of the county in which he intends to engage in such business, the name to be entered upon a book in the judge's office, to be known as the junk dealers' book, and paying to the judge the registration fee as provided in Code Section
43-22-3
.

sections.label: Section 43-22-4 - Written consent to enter another's property
sections.text: It shall be unlawful for any person, firm, or corporation or officer thereof or agent or employee of such person, firm, or corporation who is engaged in business as a junk dealer to enter upon the lands of another person, without the written consent of the owner or tenant in possession of such land, for the purpose of buying junk, or soliciting for the purpose of buying junk, or, after entering upon such land, to purchase or offer to purchase junk in any manner whatsoever.

dropped.label: Section 43-22-3 - Registration fee
dropped.reason: Administrative fee structure and receipt procedures unrelated to scope of practice or qualifications.

dropped.label: Section 43-22-5 - Penalty
dropped.reason: Penalty provision for violations is administrative enforcement rather than scope or qualification requirement.
